title: Choose Unprompted's visual world
question: Round three. Two pins held. The roll assigned The Display Case.

options.label: The Display Case
options.lineage: The card shop counter: cards laid on felt under glass, handwritten price tags, graded slabs racked on the wall behind, the top shelf you have to ask to see
options.thesis: Placement is the verdict. What the machine puts in the front row is what it recommends.
options.viewport: This week's case: brands laid out in ranked positions under glass, each with a handwritten figure, the front row holding whoever the machines named first.
options.risk: Honest reservation: a display case is a snapshot and this product is fundamentally a series. It has no native vocabulary for repeated measurement or spread, and warm glass-and-felt fights the modern, agentic coloring you asked for.

options.label: Used-Future Crew Terminal
options.lineage: Working starship terminal: green and amber phosphor on curved CRT, stencilled equipment codes, striped hazard plates
options.thesis: You key a query and the glass answers in typed capitals, one line at a time.
options.case: Held. Query-and-answer grammar fits the name, and phosphor plus amber is a real two-role system rather than decorative glow.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.lineage: Early one-bit computing: dithered grays, title bars and close boxes, marching-ants selections, 32-pixel icons
options.thesis: Two colors, honest chrome, and a selection border that never stops walking.
options.case: Held. Unbeatable tabular legibility on a phone and inherently screenshot-friendly, which is exactly the hobbyist's scene.

options.label: Algorave Source Floor
options.lineage: Live-coded music: projected source edited mid-performance, phosphor green and magenta syntax on projector black, the pattern about to change flashing amber before it sounds
options.thesis: The query is visible, the output is live, and you can watch the thing that decides change in front of you.
options.case: The closest card to what you keep reaching for: a screen world that is modern rather than retro. It is the only direction here where the prompt itself is the spectacle, which suits a publication named Unprompted, and amber-before-it-changes is a genuinely useful state for a chart that updates weekly.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.lineage: A small aircraft's night instrument panel: six luminous gauges, matte black, radium-green needles, amber and red reserved strictly for caution
options.thesis: Six readings that agree with each other, scanned in a practiced ritual, with nothing visible outside the glass.
options.case: The best dark mode in the deck by a distance, and the most disciplined colour system: black panel, luminous white, amber and red only when something is wrong. That is modern and agentic without touching the neon-on-black cliché. Weakness is warmth, it will never be playful.

options.label: Manga Screentone Page
options.lineage: The weekly manga page: screentone gradients standing in for every material, speed lines bending panel space, bleeds breaking the gutter, sound effects drawn as characters
options.thesis: A weekly page with real drama in its panels, where solid black is saved for the decisive beat.
options.case: The most culturally native card to a Pokémon audience and the highest energy in the deck, which serves the heavy-animation brief better than anything else here. Screentone encodes values without needing colour at all. The tension is that it is deliberately monochrome, so your agentic colouring would have to arrive as one imported accent.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The analytics dashboard every AI-visibility tool ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Dark navy ground, card grid, a line chart hero, one accent gradient, clean sans throughout.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Profound, Peec and Otterly, which is the exact comparison this product exists to escape.
